sections.h2: How fast can a Colleyville home be sold?
sections.html:
A cash purchase can wrap up on a schedule you set, while a standard listing in a city of expensive homes tends to take longer and may bring more. Colleyville owners weigh both.

Colleyville is in northeastern Tarrant County, and nearly every household owns its home. That leaves few investor-owned rentals and a market of larger, long-held houses.

  • Cash purchase: the house is taken as it stands, with no showings or lender delays.
  • Listing: the best route for a house in strong condition, with inspections and negotiated repairs.
  • Private sale: workable with a written contract and a title company.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Colleyville homes?
sections.html:
They describe a wealthy, settled city. QuickFacts estimates 25,727 residents for July 1, 2025, which is 1.2% below the April 2020 base, and counts 9,072 households averaging 2.86 people.

Owner costs with a mortgage are printed as $4,000+ a month, and costs without a mortgage as $1,500+. Persons in poverty are 2.5%, and 94.1% of residents kept the same address from the prior year, so houses seldom change hands. One resident in five is at least 65, which makes estate settlement and downsizing frequent reasons to sell.

The Handbook of Texas says the area was first settled in the 1850s and grew from small communities named Spring Garden, Pleasant Run, Pleasant Glade and Red Rock, later Bransford. A physician, Hilburn Howard Colley, settled in Bransford and his name was attached to a community around a store founded in 1914, becoming Coleysville and later Colleyville.

The entry says growth came mainly from proximity to Fort Worth, where most residents worked. Colleyville was incorporated on January 10, 1956, had 1,491 residents by 1964, and counted 12,724 in 1990 and 19,636 in 2000. In the early 1980s the town divided over whether to allow only costly single-family homes on large lots or smaller lots and multifamily housing.

That debate helps explain today's mix: large lots, high values and few rentals. The Census page lists 13.12 square miles of land and 1,986.2 people per square mile in 2020.

sections.h2: How do Colleyville schools and neighbors affect a sale?
sections.html:
Buyers of larger homes look at schools first. Colleyville Heritage High School belongs to Grapevine-Colleyville Independent School District and describes itself as a UIL 5A school with a National Blue Ribbon designation and the Panthers as its mascot.

Census figures reinforce why: 99.1% of adults 25 and older finished high school, 69.1% hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and the mean commute is 24.1 minutes. The Handbook places the city north of Bedford and south of Southlake, with Grapevine and Euless to the east, a useful way to describe the location to out-of-area buyers.

sections.h2: What are the Tarrant County tax dates for a Colleyville owner?
sections.html:
The county tax office has bills going out around October 1, with January 31 the last day before delinquency and February 1 the day penalty and interest start. Penalty begins at 6 percent and climbs monthly to 12 percent in July, while interest adds 1 percent monthly.

On July 1 delinquent accounts move to tax attorneys, who can add up to 20 percent. Half payments are due November 30 and June 30, and the over-65 and disability quarterly plan falls on the last day of January, March, May and July. Exemption filings at Tarrant Appraisal District close April 30 and protests May 15.

sections.h2: How is a homestead exemption filed with Tarrant Appraisal District?
sections.html:
Filing is free. You can use the district's online form or print form 50-114 and mail or email it. A Texas driver's license or ID with the home address is required.

Someone who buys and moves in can claim the exemption from the move-in date when the previous owner had none that year. The exemption also caps yearly appraisal growth at 10 percent, with exceptions for improvements and added land.

Heir property needs an ownership affidavit, the prior owner's death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation, and each other heir living there signs an authorization.

sections.h2: How do exemptions for older owners work here?
sections.html: With a fifth of residents 65 or older, many Colleyville owners hold a school tax ceiling. The Comptroller describes an extra school exemption of $60,000 and says the ceiling can follow the owner to another Texas homestead. A surviving spouse who is 55 or older may keep it. Ask the district before selling whether yours would transfer.

sections.h2: What happens to taxes when a Colleyville house closes?
sections.html: The title company splits the year between buyer and seller. A lien attaches every January 1, and the Comptroller says the January owner remains liable. If back taxes exist, the closing agent pays them from sale funds, so request a certificate from the county before accepting an offer.

sections.h2: Can heirs sell a Colleyville house quickly?
sections.html: They can once title is clear. Texas allows four years after death to probate a will, and a small estate affidavit is limited to $75,000 excluding the homestead. Other routes are a muniment of title, an executor's deed, or a transfer on death deed recorded before the owner died. An affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement that third parties may decline.

sections.h2: What if a Colleyville borrower falls behind?
sections.html: Texas servicers generally wait until a loan is over 120 days delinquent. A default notice gives 20 days to reinstate, and the sale notice follows with at least 21 days before an auction on a first Tuesday. Closing a sale first avoids the auction.

faqs.q: Is selling without an agent common in Colleyville?
faqs.a: It is possible when the house is in good condition and you can manage showings and paperwork. A title company still prepares the deed and splits the tax year.

faqs.q: When does a Colleyville buyer get the homestead exemption?
faqs.a: From the move-in date, when the seller had not claimed one that year, according to Tarrant Appraisal District.

faqs.q: Where is a Colleyville protest filed?
faqs.a: At Tarrant Appraisal District, by May 15 for the current year according to the county tax office dates page.

faqs.q: What if taxes on a Colleyville house are late?
faqs.a: Penalty climbs monthly to 12 percent in July and interest adds 1 percent monthly, so get a payoff figure from the county and expect to pay it at closing.

faqs.q: Can an heir sign a Colleyville deed before probate ends?
faqs.a: Usually not. The buyer's title company wants a court order, an executor's authority or a recorded transfer on death deed.
